These assemblies, modeled as internuncial pools, allow for dynamic reconfiguration of neural pathways to support higher-order cognition. The process is inherently thermodynamically limited, with information loss occurring at each stage—phonetic, semantic, and behavioral—consistent with the second law of thermodynamics. The behavioral translation stage then maps these semantic constructs into observable actions, constrained by system entropy and available energy. Failure modes include memory saturation, synaptic threshold mismatch, and entropy overflow, all of which degrade the fidelity of semantic-to-behavioral translation.
